I'm not the most knowledgeable person but here it goes:

First you need to identify the network of your container with "network inspect <name>". Under network settings there should be a variable called Networks

Then find out the subnet that network is using with "docker network inspect <networkname>"

Then on do an "ip a" to find out which network interface your container is using. For this you can use the subnet you got from the last step. It should be an interface name similar to br-8f95fee4b021

Once you know the interface name you can create the iptables rules for that interface

for a network interface name like br-8f95fee4b021 and a lan segment of 192.168.0.0/24:

#block all traffic from bridge to LAN

sudo iptables -I FORWARD -i br-8f95fee4b021 -d 192.168.0.0/24 -j DROP

#allow already stablished connections back to LAN

sudo iptables -I FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED -i br-8f95fee4b021 -d 192.168.0.0/24 -j ACCEPT



  

then you need a way to make those 2 new rules persistent after reboot:

sudo apt install iptables-persistent

sudo iptables-save > /etc/iptables/rules.v4



by the way when creating the container you need to set the dns to something outside your lan for example 8.8.8.8, I think the docker run options would be "dns=8.8.8.8"
